pr_title: bluetooth: host: Fix NULL pointer dereference in bt_conn_auth_cb_overlay
pr_body:
There is a check in bt_conn_auth_cb_overlayfunction which validates if content of the callback structure is correct, but there is no NULL-check on the structure pointer itself, which could result in NULL pointer dereference.

It should be possible to set the callback structure pointer to `NULL` using bt_conn_auth_cb_overlay function if the application requires ex. Just Works pairing for one Bluetooth identity and global callbacks are configured for advanced pairing scheme (like Passkey Display) for other Bluetooth identity.

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/57941

issue_context.title: bluetooth: host: null pointer dereference possible in `bt_conn_auth_cb_overlay()`
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Currently, there is a way to overlay authentication callbacks for a Bluetooth LE connection using `bt_conn_auth_cb_overlay() `.
There is a check in mentioned function which validates if content of the callback structure is correct, but there is no `NULL`-check on the structure pointer itself.
It should be possible to set the callback structure pointer to `NULL` if the application requires ex. Just Works pairing for one Bluetooth identity and global callbacks are configured for advanced pairing scheme (like Passkey Display) for other Bluetooth identity.

**Impact**
Null pointer dereference, crashes.

**Environment:**
 - Commit SHA or Version used: 21b9a1c8239637bbecd0b74381f3d8fb069a47b3

review_comments: Please split `bt_conn_auth_cb_overlayfunction` in the commit message into 2 words.

Change looks good to be, but also consider 
1) Use CHECKIF for the `cb == NULL` check 
2) Also add a check for `conn == NULL`

1. It is our intention to allow setting callback structure pointer to `NULL` as stated in the PR description, so I did not apply that suggestion.
2. Added.

If the intention is to allow setting `cb == NULL`, should `bt_smp_auth_cb_overlay` be modified to set `smp->auth_cb` to `BT_SMP_AUTH_CB_UNINITIALIZED` if `cb == NULL`? 


If `bt_smp_auth_cb_overlay` is currently called with `cb == NULL`, then `smp->auth_cb` is set to NULL, right? I think that will break all sort of stuff as the return value of `latch_auth_cb` is not checked for NULL.

Hi @Thalley
The `smp->auth_cb` set to `NULL` are actually considered a proper value in this context (they represent lack of hardware capabilities that could be used for Bluetooth authentication). The uninitialized value is used to mark callbacks as not yet set to a valid value.
The `latch_auth_cb` sets them either to the authentication callbacks assigned per connection or to global authentication callbacks if the per-connection callbacks are not set. The `latch_auth_cb` modifies the set of callbacks used in the SMP module only once in connection's lifetime.

@MarekPieta You are correct - Just had another look at it :) 

I also see that `smp_auth_cb = latch_auth_cb(smp);` is usually checked for NULL as well. 

There are a few cases, `smp_pairing_random`, `smp_public_key_periph`, `smp_public_key` and `smp_keypress_notif` where we access `smp_auth_cb` without checking for NULL. 

Are these OK to run without a NULL check, or will it break stuff it `cb == NULL`?

IIRC the `NULL` check was not here since the beginning (it was even not here when we used a single global authentication callbacks). I understood that implementation assumes that the callbacks cannot be NULL at this point and it's ensured by state checks (still it may be worth asserting to ensure we are on the safe side).

@Thalley, according to my understanding, the overlay API is as secure as the global instance `bt_auth` of the authentication callbacks that can be registered with the standard `bt_conn_auth_cb_register` API. If the API user does not register callbacks with the `bt_conn_auth_cb_register`, the `bt_auth` pointer is equal to NULL as well.

I think that implementation hardening in this area is outside the scope of this PR and is not strictly related to the `bt_conn_auth_cb_overlay` API. We would like to port this bug fix to our upcoming NCS release (we are at the rc1 stage currently). It would be great if we could finalize this review within this week (release deadlines) as the fix is very small.
Agreed, and roger that :) (also why I didn't mark my review as "request changes" ;) )
